objective: The last day of a date range is left out. `stockroom sales --orders F --to 2024-02-14` does not count the orders placed on 2024-02-14, and asking an order book for the orders between two dates omits the orders placed on the end date. Both dates of a range are included (an order placed on the start date or on the end date belongs to it), orders come back oldest first with ties in insertion order, and a range that contains no dates (the end is before the start) contains no orders. In the command, `--from` alone means there is no upper limit and `--to` alone means there is no lower limit.
acceptance: Orders between 2024-01-08 and 2024-01-19 of the sample file are A-1001 and A-1002; between 2024-01-09 and 2024-02-14 they are A-1002, A-1003 and A-1004; between 2024-03-21 and 2024-03-21 only A-1006; between 2024-03-02 and 2024-12-31 A-1005 and A-1006
A one-day range returns that day's orders in insertion order, and a longer range returns orders oldest first with orders of one day in insertion order
A range with no orders, a range ending before the first order, a range starting after the last order and a reversed range (end before start) return an empty list

`stockroom sales --to 2024-02-14` on the sample file prints `3 orders, 1 cancelled` and `Revenue: $122.35`; `--to 2024-02-13` prints `2 orders, 1 cancelled` and `Revenue: $67.95`; `--to 2024-03-21` prints `5 orders, 1 cancelled` and `Revenue: $149.65`
`stockroom sales --from D --to D` counts only the orders placed on day D: 2024-03-21 gives `1 order, 0 cancelled` and `Revenue: $12.50`, 2024-01-08 gives `1 order, 0 cancelled` and `Revenue: $33.95`

With only `--from`, every order on or after that day is counted, even one placed on 9999-12-31; with only `--to`, every order up to and including that day is counted, and a `--to` before the first order gives `0 orders, 0 cancelled` and `Revenue: $0.00`
